request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now turn columns of the people list on and off, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works:**
- **Storage:** each user's choice is saved on the server under their own name, not per sheet, so it stays the same when they reload or switch sheets. I followed the existing per-user locale setting. Only the columns a user has switched off are stored, in a new table (`V89__user_column.sql`). A user who never touches the boxes sees every column.
- **Server:** `GET /api/columns` returns the columns the signed-in user has switched off, and `POST /api/columns` with `{column, shown}` switches one column on or off. An unknown column name is refused. Changing a column writes no audit line and is allowed while viewing a sheet as of a past date, the same as the locale setting. The code is in `net.officefloor.hq.app.columns`.
- **Screen:** there is a row of checkboxes (`column-<key>`) in `features/columns/columns.slot.tsx`. A box takes effect as soon as it's clicked, without waiting for the server. If the save fails, an error shows (`columns-error`) and the boxes are reset to what the server has stored.
- **Hiding cells:** a small `Col` wrapper removes a switched-off column's cell from every row, and also its heading so the table stays lined up. The people table, totals, summary, rollups and header counts are worked out exactly as before.

**One addition to the request:** the test also switches off `excess`, which isn't in the request's list, so `excess` is a choosable column as well (15 in all).

Only the value cell disappears when a column is off. The action controls that sit next to it, such as the hold and retire buttons or the alias input, stay on screen.
